summary: A concrete light and fog-signal house at the north tip of Admiralty Island, built 1924 after years as an unwatched acetylene light; now owned by a non-profit.

lens.where: removed from cupola in 1950s; fate not found

access.note: Reached only by water or air; USLHS records not open to public; Alaska Lighthouse Association owner, access by arrangement per LighthouseFriends; current status unconfirmed.

notes_for_editor: Staffing end date disputed (1911 vs 1917). Bulletin 1924 diaphone item gives December 22 but no year in the readable text; the year of installation (1923 or 1924) is not stated in the story. 1931 Bulletin hit is fuzzy OCR. Current ownership/access unconfirmed: LighthouseFriends says Association website inactive. Corrections to consider: record structures say 1924 tower 15 m; NRHP gives roughly 18 ft tower atop a building. McLeod child's injury is from LighthouseFriends only (second-hand compilation). Roster lines after 1960 (Coast Guard crews and later head keepers listed by the USLHS archive) are deliberately not carried into the roster under the living-people rule. Opening sentence no longer says white/small (not sourced). Building dimensions differ: nomination 34x20 ft, Lighthousefriends 20x36 ft.
